summary: PICA's visa table gives the rule nationality by nationality. Among the passports it lists as needing no visa are the United States (for 6 months), Canada, the United Kingdom and Commonwealth countries such as Australia and India; some are allowed 90 days, such as Germany, Brazil and South Korea, and others 30, such as France, Spain and Japan. Holders of Haitian ordinary passports need a visa, and for some nationalities, such as Armenia and Georgia, the visa may be obtained at the port of entry. PICA lists a completed and signed Immigration/Customs C5 form, either online or a physical form, among the documents required on arrival.

conditionalWaivers.text: Tourists from Albania, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Kazakhstan, North Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Romania, Serbia and Honduras who hold a valid US, Canadian, UK or Schengen visa may enter Jamaica without a Jamaican visa for 30 days or less. All except Honduras must also carry proof of vaccination against measles, rubella and polio.

processing.text: The processing time for visa applications submitted to the Embassy is between ten to fifteen business days.

name.text: The requirements for the Jamaican tourist visa are as follows:

method.text: Nationals of certain countries require, in addition to travel documents, an entry visa. This is normally issued, on application, by a Jamaican Consular office.

fee.notes: PICA fee schedule. A person at the port of entry who should have obtained an entry visa prior to arrival pays US$350.00 instead.

name.text: All foreign nationals who are transiting through Jamaica for a period not exceeding seventy-two (72) hours do not require a transit visa except holders of a Cuban passport.

fee.notes: PICA's processing fee for an extension of stay, from its Immigration Processing Fee schedule. The schedule lists JM$50,000.00 for persons who wish to extend their stay beyond the visa exemption period. PICA says Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 12 months' stay as visitors and non-Commonwealth citizens a maximum of 6 months.

processing.text: Extensions of stay are processed within three (3) working days for all the categories.

extendable.text: Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 12 months stay on the island and Non-Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 6 months stay on the island as a visitor.

name.text: A foreign national seeking to extend their stay in the island, can do so by submitting an application for an extension.

passportValidity.text: Jamaica's Embassy in Washington says the travel document should have at least six months' validity. The UK Foreign Office says your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay and have 2 blank pages for entry and exit stamps.

source.name: Embassy of Jamaica, Washington DC — Visitors to Jamaica: requirements for entry

conflict.name: UK FCDO — Jamaica entry requirements
conflict.states: Your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay and have 2 blank pages.

source.name: UK FCDO — Jamaica entry requirements

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (yellow card)
vaccinations.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must have a certificate proving yellow fever vaccination if you are coming from a country listed as a transmission risk.

source.name: UK FCDO — Jamaica entry requirements

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states whether travel insurance is required to enter Jamaica. The UK Foreign Office advises checking before you travel that you have appropriate travel insurance for local treatment or unexpected medical evacuation.

source.name: UK FCDO travel advice — Jamaica health

onwardTicket.text: Jamaica's Embassy in Washington says visitors must be in possession of a return or round-trip ticket to another country to which they are admissible.

source.name: Embassy of Jamaica, Washington DC (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade) — Requirements for entry into Jamaica

proofOfFunds.text: Jamaica's Embassy in Washington says visitors are required to show evidence of sufficient funds to support themselves during their stay. No official source we could read states an amount.

source.name: Embassy of Jamaica, Washington DC (Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade) — Requirements for entry into Jamaica

declarations.name: Immigration/Customs (C5) form
declarations.submitWindow: Online before arrival where possible; a paper form is also accepted
declarations.text: PICA says all arriving travellers must present a completed and signed Immigration/Customs C5 form, either online or a physical form. The UK Foreign Office says to complete it online where possible before you arrive.

source.name: PICA — Travel documents required

currencyLimits.text: The UK Foreign Office says cash or travellers cheques worth 10,000 US dollars or more must be declared on your C5 form, and that you will also have to complete the Financial Investigation Division Cross Border Form. The C5 form at enterjamaica.gov.jm asks whether you are carrying currency or monetary instruments over US$10,000 or equivalent.

source.name: UK FCDO — Jamaica entry requirements

notes: The Government of Canada says entering Jamaica with a firearm or even a single round of ammunition is considered a serious crime.

The UK FCDO says smoking marijuana (ganja) is illegal in Jamaica: possession of up to 2 ounces brings a fine of 500 Jamaican dollars, and severe penalties apply to all other drug offences, including attempting to export narcotics. The Government of Canada says departing visitors are thoroughly screened for drug possession.

The UK FCDO says it is illegal to bring meat and dairy products into Jamaica, and the C5 form at enterjamaica.gov.jm asks travellers to declare fruits, plants, vegetables, meat, animal products and other foods.
The Government of Canada says it is illegal to wear, buy or sell army or police camouflage clothing.

overstay.text: An alien found in Jamaica after the period limited by the conditions of leave to land is deemed, for the purposes of the Aliens Act, to be an alien refused leave to land. The Government of Canada says overstaying a visa or entry stamp is a criminal offence and can lead to prison time, heavy fines and deportation. The UK government says that if you overstay without authority, you could be fined or arrested.

driving.text: The UN treaty records list Jamaica as a party to the 1949 Geneva Convention on Road Traffic (succession, 9 August 1963). Jamaica's Road Traffic Act, 2018 (s. 41) says a driving permit issued by another party to the 1949 Geneva Convention while the holder was not resident in Jamaica, and a driver's licence granted in any prescribed country, count as a Jamaican permit or licence for the class of vehicle they cover. A foreign licence counts until it expires, until the holder leaves Jamaica, or for twelve months from the holder's arrival on proof of entry, whichever comes first, and never covers driving passengers or goods for hire or reward. No official source we could read lists the prescribed countries. The Act sets the blood-alcohol limit at 80 milligrammes of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood; for the holder of a learner's permit, and for the holder of a driver's licence during the first twelve months of the licence, it says the breath alcohol concentration must not exceed 0.01 per cent or 10 micrograms of alcohol per 100 millilitres of breath. Canada's travel advice says you can drive with a valid Canadian driver's licence for up to 6 months, and the UK says a UK driving licence can be used for up to 6 months; the Act, which ranks above that advice, sets twelve months for licences from prescribed countries.

tips.text: PICA accepts the Immigration/Customs C5 form online or as a physical form; the online form is at enterjamaica.gov.jm, a PICA site. The UK Foreign Office says to complete it online where possible before you arrive.
The Government of Canada says entering Jamaica with a firearm or even a single round of ammunition is a serious crime.

The UK FCDO says it is illegal to smoke marijuana (ganja) in Jamaica, that possession of up to 2 ounces brings a fine, and that severe penalties apply to all other drug offences, including attempting to export narcotics. The Government of Canada says departing visitors are thoroughly screened for drug possession.

The Government of Canada says traffic drives on the left, advises against unmarked taxis and recommends taxis authorised by the Jamaica Union of Travellers Association (JUTA), identified by red and white “PP” licence plates; taxis aren't metered, so agree on the fare before departure. The UK FCDO recommends Jamaican Tourist Board (JTB) approved taxis, whose drivers display a blue JTB sticker.
The UK FCDO says arrival and departure taxes are usually included in the cost of your ticket, and that your carrier can advise you if you are unsure.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Jamaica?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport; PICA's visa table gives the rule nationality by nationality. It lists no visa required for the United States for 6 months; for 90 days for, among others, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, Brazil, Mexico and South Korea; for 30 days for France, Spain, Portugal and Japan; and with no period for Canada, the United Kingdom and Commonwealth countries such as Australia and India. For Armenia, Georgia and some other nationalities a visa is required but may be obtained at the port of entry, where PICA's fee schedule lists the Port of Entry Visa at US$100. Others need a visa, which Jamaica's Embassy in Washington says is normally issued, on application, by a Jamaican Consular office.

faq.question: What is the Jamaica C5 form and is it mandatory?
faq.answer: The C5 is Jamaica's Immigration/Customs form. PICA lists a completed and signed C5 form, either online or a physical form, among the documents required of foreign nationals and of Jamaican citizens on arrival. The UK government says you must make a customs declaration before entering Jamaica and should complete the C5 online where possible before you arrive.

faq.question: Do I still need a Jamaica Travel Authorization?
faq.answer: No official source we could read mentions a Jamaica Travel Authorization. PICA lists the documents required for the immigration interview on arrival as a valid passport or other acceptable travel document, a valid Jamaican entry visa if applicable, and a completed and signed Immigration/Customs C5 form, either online or a physical form.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Jamaica without a visa?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport: PICA's visa-requirements table allows 30 days for some nationalities, 90 for others and 6 months for the United States. Jamaica's Embassy in Washington says the decision on admission and length of stay rests with the Immigration Officer at the port of entry, and the UK says the date you must leave is stamped on your passport. PICA says an extension should be applied for before the landing time expires, and that Commonwealth citizens are allowed a maximum of 12 months' stay as visitors and non-Commonwealth citizens a maximum of 6 months.

faq.question: How much passport validity do I need for Jamaica?
faq.answer: Jamaica's Embassy in Washington says the travel document should have at least six months' validity. The UK Foreign Office says your passport must be valid for the duration of your stay and have 2 blank pages for entry and exit stamps.

faq.question: Is Jamaica safe for tourists?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says crime and homicide rates are high, with gang violence and shootings mostly in inner-city areas, and that tourist areas are not usually affected by gang-related crime. It lists Kingston, Spanish Town, Savanna-la-Mar and parts of Montego Bay, advises not walking in isolated areas or on deserted beaches, even during the day, and advises using reputable, licensed providers, including for taxis.
